note: Spelling dictation task, Study 2 (N=786 ids live: 372 Stetson college, 414 MTurk; 72 items; 56,592 rows). The IRW item code IS the Study2.xlsx column header (data/spelling assessment_study2.R selects abhorrent:warranty and pivots them straight into item), and each header is the target word itself, so item_text reproduces the code verbatim; no code->text inference. Live per-item n and per-item sum of resp match Study2.xlsx exactly for all 72 items (n 780-786 per item). item_text is the word SPOKEN to participants, not text they read. instructions is the paper's Study 1 procedure sentence ('Participants were instructed to listen to each word spoken three (or four) times and to spell that word by typing it into the space provided.'), carried to Study 2 because the paper says 'The same set of words from the first study was used to validate the spelling measure' and Study 2 does not restate the spelling procedure; Study 2's audio screening item ('Participants listened to an audio file of the word apple') is consistent with aural presentation. It is third-person description, not on-screen wording, which is not in the deposit. resp is binary accuracy; option_text Incorrect=0 / Correct=1, correct_response=1 (same shape as spelling_assessment_study1). Direction confirmed three ways, not assumed from the sibling: (a) the file's own Best20AvgScore satisfies 20*Best20AvgScore - (sum of the 19 deposited Best-20 words) in {0,1} for all 776 non-missing respondents (212 zero, 564 one), i.e. it is a proportion of words scored 1; (b) AvgScore correlates 0.99 with each respondent's mean resp over the 72 words; (c) per-item Study 2 accuracy correlates 0.96 with Study 1 accuracy on the same 72 words (range 30% apocryphal to 94%). SOURCE/DEPOSIT FACTS (not IRW mapping defects): Study2.xlsx is 786 x 84, not 86 columns as the batch_344 handoff note said, and carries 72 of the 109 Study 1 words; the other 37 (accessory, accomplice, anatomic, antecedent, assessor, assimilate, avalanche, buoyancy, cartesian, cartilage, dysentery, filament, immodest, impotent, irreverent, labyrinth, lucidity, masquerade, mayonnaise, misogynist, moustache, nonchalant, pacifier, palliative, parachute, permeate, pheasant, propitiate, pseudonym, quiescent, repertoire, rigidity, stiletto, stratify, subtlety, tranquil, vehicular) are absent from the deposit. They were apparently administered: AvgScore is a multiple of 1/109 for 97% of respondents, and the Best-20 identity in (a) needs a 20th 0/1 word -- buoyancy, which the authors' own Study 2 code (Lexical Expertise Code.R line 159) selects from Study2.xlsx but which the deposited file lacks, so that code cannot run on the deposit as posted. Supplemental Materials.xlsx's STUDY 2 ALL/MTURK/COLLEGE blocks hold factor loadings for the Best-20/Best-10 sets (item labels copied from Study 1's Best-20 list, including buoyancy), not per-item accuracy, so they were not usable as a direction check (correcting the batch_344 handoff note). Rights: the stimuli are ordinary English words from Burt & Tate (2002); no restriction on the words located or plausible.
public_note: Words were presented aurally and typed by participants; item_text is the target word, and instructions paraphrase the procedure as the paper reports it for Study 1, whose word set Study 2 reused. The deposit (and so this table) holds 72 of the 109 words the authors appear to have administered.
